items.title: NERAI Maritime Weekly
events: Iran Brokers Saudi-Houthi Ceasefire Talks; $1bn Deal Reported
Saudi Coalition Intercepts Three Houthi Missiles and Four Drones
Singapore Minister Warns Hormuz Crisis Is Structural, Not Episodic
UK Issues New Designation Under Sudan Sanctions Regulations 2020
Indonesia: Tanker Used Ship-to-Ship Transfer to Smuggle Ketamine
items.summary: The week was dominated by two converging threads at the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea: kinetic Houthi activity continued with further missile and drone intercepts, while Iran-brokered diplomacy — including a reported Saudi $1 bn ceasefire offer to the Houthis — signalled the first substantive de-escalation probe of the crisis. Singapore's Energy Minister publicly framed the Hormuz disruption as a structural, recurring risk rather than a passing episode, a posture that tracks NERAI's elevated 4-week Hormuz disruption probability of 50%. On the compliance front, the UK added a new designation under its Sudan sanctions regulations.
